text:
Amina: Quick note - the new "next-rag-starter" we've been shipping to docs is tripping users during onboarding when they try the eval harness on Vercel Edge.
Carlos: Repro steps?
Amina: Clone starter, set RW_API_KEY, deploy to Vercel Edge. Trigger /api/query which proxies to an LlamaIndex-backed RAG flow and then run the eval harness. The harness often reports missing embeddings and 401s on the first downstream call.
Ruth: Which SDK + starter SHA?
Amina: SDK v0.10.3, starter at commit 9c7d2. Next 13.5.4. Happens on vercel dev --edge and real preview.
Vikram: Any logs or short stack traces?
Amina: Snippet: 
```
WARN sdk: auth: token refresh started
Error: embeddings: no vector returned
    at buildIndex (/workspace/lib/ingest.js:48:9)
TypeError: fetch is not a function
    at sendTelemetry (/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/telemetry.js:22:11)
```
Carlos: So two things: missing global fetch in the bundled edge function (bundler polyfilled differently), and auth refresh race where first request still fails.
Ruth: Does the starter call await init(...) in the handler? Edge cold starts need the explicit await to ensure SDK finished setup.
Amina: The example used `init({apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY})` w/o await to keep README short.
Vikram: Oof. On Node that usually works due to persistent modules. On Edge cold start the init sequence can be interrupted. But we should make SDK robust: if fetch missing, avoid throwing; instead queue telemetry and flush at end-of-request or skip gracefully with a warning.
Carlos: Also the embedding backend call returning empty vector looks like the auth token wasn't attached. If refresh happened, the first in-flight request might still use old header. We should make refresh atomic per-invocation and provide optional request-scoped tokenProvider in init.
Amina: I hacked the handler to: 
```js
export default async function handler(req) {
  await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, tokenProvider: { get: () => req.cookies.rw_tkn, set: () => {} } })
  return await query(req.body)
}
```
Amina: With that change the 401-on-first-call went away, but the telemetry error remained until I added a small fetch polyfill in the bundle.
Ruth: We don't want customers to need manual polyfills. SDK should detect a missing global fetch and use the platform fetch when available, otherwise fall back to a lightweight fetch shim that uses Request/Response if possible. Also add a clear console message recommending targeting the web build for edge.
Vikram: Agreed. Action items: (1) SDK: detect missing fetch + prefer platform web APIs, (2) SDK: make init idempotent + accept tokenProvider for request-scoped auth, (3) samples: update examples to `await init(...)` and show tokenProvider pattern in the Edge README.
Carlos: I'll open a tiny sample PR to make the handler explicit and add a short note about Edge vs Server tradeoffs in the quickstart.
kevin-ci: Created ticket DEVEX-4205: "next-rag-starter - edge onboarding: fetch polyfill + auth race" assigned to @Vikram and @Carlos.
Amina: Pushed logs and a minimal repro gist to the ticket: https://gist.github.com/redwood-repro/next-rag-edge-4205.
devex-bot: Linked the ticket to SDK issue SDK-5234 for tokenProvider + fetch detection.
Ruth: I'll draft the SDK PR to add tokenProvider and the fetch guard today. Will include unit tests that simulate missing global.fetch and missing setTimeout to validate retry/backoff fallbacks.
Carlos: Sample PR incoming to swap init to await + comment about tokenProvider. I'll also add a small CI smoke test that runs the eval harness in node mode to catch the obvious regression early.
Amina: Thanks team. Will re-run the harness after PRs land and report back.
Carlos: :thumbsup:
_meta: devex thread: next rag starter onboarding edge auth/fetch parity
